```{r setup,include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE)
library(capnet); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(lubridate)
repo_root <- normalizePath("../..")
source("helpers.R"); source("experiments.R")
results_dir <- file.path(repo_root,"manuscript/results")
results <- if(params$rerun) paper_wiki() else readRDS(file.path(results_dir,"wiki.rds"))
```

## Data and week-like batching

Daily English Wikipedia pageviews for 30 articles span 2022-01-01 through
2024-12-31 in the bundled `inst/extdata/wiki_traffic.csv`. Covariates are the
current day's article views, in thousands; the response is the **next day's**
aggregate count. The aggregate is omitted from the predictors because it is
the sum of the article series. The final covariate row is dropped because
its next-day target is unavailable.

```{r data}
wiki <- paper_wiki_data()
articles <- setdiff(names(wiki),c("date","target"))
range(wiki$date)
calc_moments(wiki[,articles])
```

Models use one-year training windows refit monthly. Evaluation covariates
span 2023-01-01 through 2024-12-30, with targets through 2024-12-31. We retain
`walk = 5` for computational efficiency as a **five-day, week-like conditional
batch**. Slices contain five consecutive daily rows (including weekends),
restart each month, and may end with a shorter slice.

All covariates in the slice enter the penalty together. Responses in that
slice do not enter fitting. The five-row procedure is therefore conditional
on the batch's covariates, not a five-day-ahead forecast issued using only
information known on its first day. It is also not a weekly aggregate target:
scoring remains at the daily next-day-count level. A deployment that does not
know the batch covariates must supply predictor scenarios or use `walk = 1`.
This distinction lets us retain the faster experiment without overstating
its forecast-origin information set.

## Estimation

We use the Poisson log-link loss as a working conditional-mean objective,
not a claim of a calibrated Poisson count distribution. `lambda = 0` isolates
the contribution penalty; alpha is immaterial. The feature-specific ceiling
is three times the absolute **training univariate Poisson slope**. This
differs from the finance correlation rule. The gamma grid is fixed at
`c(10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000)`.

```{r definitions}
wiki_L
paper_wiki
```

The ordinary capnet fit with gamma zero supplies the uncapped baseline.
Post-fit capping clips its slope contributions on the log-mean scale, retains
the intercept, and exponentiates to get predicted counts. Batches are evaluated
serially in this reproduction; changing independent execution order is not a
statistical change to the experiment.

## Scores and diagnostics

The score is **squared-error out-of-sample R-squared**, not a deviance-based
pseudo-R-squared. `calc_oos_r2` compares summed squared errors to an expanding
mean of preceding evaluation responses and drops the first observation.

```{r scores}
summary_table <- paper_scores(results,"date")
knitr::kable(summary_table,digits=6)
```

The complete grid is a sensitivity analysis. The plotted gamma is the one
with the largest full-window score, chosen **retrospectively**. It is not a
separately validated deployment choice, and its performance is not an unbiased
estimate of a tuning procedure's future performance.

The figure compares each method's maximum absolute feature contribution on
one shared logarithmic vertical axis. The axis compresses the isolated 2023
uncapped spike while keeping the smaller daily values visible. Its tick labels
give contribution magnitudes on the original log-mean scale.

```{r plots,fig.width=9,fig.height=5.6}
walk_scores <- summary_table |> filter(method=="Walk-forward Capnet")
best_gamma <- walk_scores$gamma[which.max(walk_scores$oos_r2)]
plots <- paper_plots(results,"date",best_gamma,window=180,wiki=TRUE)
plots$contributions
```

Rolling scores use **180 scored observations**, consistent with the original
vignette. Each window is summed directly to avoid cumulative-subtraction
cancellation after a very large forecast error leaves the window. The pooled
scores above and the 2024-only comparison below summarize predictive accuracy.
The contribution figure computes the nonnegative maximum absolute contribution
separately for each model and row, rather than tracking a reference model's
selected feature or plotting signed values.

```{r snapshot}
features <- c("google","microsoft","tesla","nvidia","chatgpt","netflix","sony","elon_musk","sam_altman","youtube")
knitr::kable(paper_snapshot(results,"date","2023-03-14",best_gamma,features),digits=3)
```

These are selected features' contributions to the log-mean; they exclude the
intercept. They are not an additive decomposition of the count forecast error.

## 2024-only robustness comparison

```{r robustness}
knitr::kable(paper_scores(results,"date",year=2024),digits=6)
```

This restricts the **same saved predictions** to covariate dates in calendar
2024 and recomputes the expanding benchmark within that subperiod. It does not
refit, retune gamma, or carry the benchmark mean over from 2023. The plotted
full-window gamma remains fixed for interpreting this comparison.

```{r numerical-checks}
stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.numeric(results$predictions$predicted))))
results$diagnostics |> group_by(method,requested_gamma) |>
  summarise(missing=sum(missing),
    reduced_rows=sum(effective_gamma<requested_gamma,na.rm=TRUE),
    unsuccessful_stops=sum(!is.na(convergence)&convergence<0&convergence != -1001),
    .groups="drop")
```

The exported mean diagnostics report held-out mean observed/predicted counts
and average Pearson-type squared residuals. They are descriptive and do not
turn the working Poisson loss into a validated full predictive distribution.

Run `bash tools/reproduce_paper.sh` from the repository root for a fresh source
install and all results. `params = list(rerun = TRUE)` reruns fitting when
rendering this report. Raw fits/predictions, the 2024-only scores, plotted
maxima, package versions, and input/source checksums are saved under
`manuscript/results/wiki*`.
